rows.ARS:
Apricot or apricot blend Floribunda.
Registration name: JACcofl
Exhibition name: Brass Band ™
rows.Origin:
Bred by Jack E. Christensen (United States, 1993).
Introduced in United States by Jackson & Perkins Co. (post 1970) in 1994 as 'Brass Band'.
rows.Bloom: Apricot or apricot blend. Mild, damask fragrance. 30 to 41 petals. Average diameter 2.75". Large, full (26-40 petals) bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b and warmer. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) . Can be grown in the ground or in a container (container requires winter protection).
rows.Breeder's notes: Yellow buds open to deep peach-colored flowers; unusual and quite striking. Blooms heavily. Fairly low. (as per JC's website).
